problem.paragraph: Find the velocity and the speed of a particle with the position function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left( \frac{2t - 1}{2t + 1} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \ln (1 - 4t^{2})\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ The speed of a particle is the magnitude of the velocity and is represented by $${ \text{‖} {r^{'}(t)} \text{‖} }.$$

exercises.paragraph: A particle moves on a circular path of radius b according to the function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = b\cos (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + b\sin (\omega t)\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ where $$\omega$$ is the angular velocity, $${{d\theta}/{dt}}.$$

problem.paragraph: Find the velocity function and show that $$\mathbf{ \text{v} }(t)$$ is always orthogonal to $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t).$$

solution.paragraph: $$r'(t)=-b\omega sin(\omega t)i+b\omega cos(\omega t)j.r'(t)=-b\omega sin(\omega t)i+b\omega cos(\omega t)j.$$ To show orthogonality, note that $$r'(t)\cdot r(t)=0.r'(t)\cdot r(t)=0.$$

problem.paragraph: Show that the speed of the particle is proportional to the angular velocity.

Find the antiderivative of $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }'(t) = \cos (2t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } - 2\sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \frac{1}{1 + t^{2}}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ that satisfies the initial condition $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(0) = 3\mathbf{ \text{i} } - 2\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$

An object starts from rest at point $$P\left( {1,2,0} \right)$$ and moves with an acceleration of $$\mathbf{ \text{a} }(t) = \mathbf{ \text{j} } + 2\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ where $$\text{‖} {\mathbf{ \text{a} }(t)} \text{‖}$$ is measured in feet per second per second. Find the location of the object after $$t = 2$$ sec.
Show that if the speed of a particle traveling along a curve represented by a vector-valued function is constant, then the velocity function is always perpendicular to the acceleration function.

solution.paragraph: $$‖v(t)‖=kv(t)\cdot v(t)=kddt(v(t)\cdot v(t))=ddtk=0v(t)\cdot v'(t)+v'(t)\cdot v(t)=02v(t)\cdot v'(t)=0v(t)\cdot v'(t)=0.‖v(t)‖=kv(t)\cdot v(t)=kddt(v(t)\cdot v(t))=ddtk=0v(t)\cdot v'(t)+v'(t)\cdot v(t)=02v(t)\cdot v'(t)=0v(t)\cdot v'(t)=0.$$ The last statement implies that the velocity and acceleration are perpendicular or orthogonal.

problem.paragraph: Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{u} }(t) = 4t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t^{3}\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ find $$\frac{d}{dt}\left( {\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) \times \mathbf{ \text{u} }(t)} \right).$$
Given $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {t + \cos t,t - \sin t} \right\rangle,$$ find the velocity and the speed at any time.
Find the velocity vector for the function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {e^{t},e^{-t},0} \right\rangle.$$
Find an equation of the tangent line to the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {e^{t},e^{-t},0} \right\rangle$$ at $$t = 0.$$
Describe and sketch the curve represented by the vector-valued function $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {6t,6t - t^{2}} \right\rangle.$$
Locate the highest point on the curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \left\langle {6t,6t - t^{2}} \right\rangle$$ and give the value of the function at this point.
